ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The distance between two parallel rails is $15\mathrm{cm}$, the mass of the metal rod MN is $\mathrm{m}=17\mathrm{g}$, its resistance $\mathrm{R}_{1}$ is $4\Omega$, the sliding rheostat $\mathrm{R}_{2}$ is connected in series with MN, the magnetic induction intensity B of the uniform magnetic field is vertically upward with a magnitude of $0.6\mathrm{T}$, the electromotive force of the power source is $E = 10\mathrm{{V}}$, and the internal resistance $\mathbf{r}=1\Omega$. When the switch S is closed, the metal rod MN remains stationary ($g=10\mathrm{m/s}^{2}$, $\sqrt{3}=1.7$).

1. If the parallel rails are smooth, find the magnitude of the Ampere force acting on the metal rod and the resistance value of $\mathrm{R}_{2}$ (retain one significant figure in the result).
2. If the parallel rails are not smooth, and the resistance of the sliding rheostat $\mathrm{R}_{2}$ is adjusted to $10\Omega$, while the metal rod MN remains stationary, determine the magnitude and direction of the frictional force acting on the metal rod.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the metal rod MN is placed horizontally across two parallel guide rails, and the guide rails form an inclined plane, marked 30° in the figure; the arrow of magnetic field B is vertically upward. The guide rails, metal rod MN, sliding rheostat R2, power supply, and switch S form a series closed circuit, and the metal rod's own resistance is R1. Reasoning: 1. When the guide rails are smooth, the metal rod MN is subject to gravity mg, supporting force, and Ampere force F. Decomposing along the direction of the guide rails, the supporting force has no component along the guide rails. From the condition of static equilibrium: F cos30° = mg sin30°, so F = mg tan30°. It is known that m=17 g=0.017 kg, g=10 m/s², mg=0.17 N, tan30°=1/√3≈1/1.7, F=0.17/1.7=0.10 N, retained to one significant figure as 0.1 N. From the Ampere force formula F=BIl, the distance between the guide rails is the effective length of the metal rod l=15 cm=0.15 m: I=F/(Bl)=0.10/(0.6×0.15)=0.10/0.09≈1.1 A. The total resistance of the circuit is E/I≈10/1.1≈9 Ω. The total series resistance r+R1+R2=1+4+R2, therefore R2≈9-1-4=4 Ω. 2. When the guide rails are rough and R2=10 Ω, the total resistance is R_total=r+R1+R2=1+4+10=15 Ω, and the current I=E/R_total=10/15=2/3 A. The magnitude of the Ampere force: F=BIl=0.6×(2/3)×0.15=0.06 N. Its component upward along the inclined plane is F cos30°=0.06×(√3/2)≈0.06×0.85=0.051 N. The component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sin30°=0.17×0.5=0.085 N. Since mg sin30° > F cos30°, the metal rod has a tendency to slide downward along the inclined plane, so the direction of static friction is upward along the inclined plane, with magnitude f=mg sin30°−F cos30°=0.085−0.051=0.034 N.

raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the metal rod MN is placed horizontally across two parallel guide rails, and the guide rails form an inclined plane, marked 30° in the figure; the arrow of magnetic field B is vertically upward. The guide rails, metal rod MN, sliding rheostat R2, power supply, and switch S form a series closed circuit, and the metal rod's own resistance is R1.

Reasoning:
1. When the guide rails are smooth, the metal rod MN is subject to gravity mg, supporting force, and Ampere force F. Decomposing along the direction of the guide rails, the supporting force has no component along the guide rails. From the condition of static equilibrium:
F cos30° = mg sin30°,
so F = mg tan30°.
It is known that m=17 g=0.017 kg, g=10 m/s², mg=0.17 N, tan30°=1/√3≈1/1.7,
F=0.17/1.7=0.10 N, retained to one significant figure as 0.1 N.

From the Ampere force formula F=BIl, the distance between the guide rails is the effective length of the metal rod l=15 cm=0.15 m:
I=F/(Bl)=0.10/(0.6×0.15)=0.10/0.09≈1.1 A.
The total resistance of the circuit is E/I≈10/1.1≈9 Ω.
The total series resistance r+R1+R2=1+4+R2, therefore
R2≈9-1-4=4 Ω.

2. When the guide rails are rough and R2=10 Ω, the total resistance is
R_total=r+R1+R2=1+4+10=15 Ω,
the current I=E/R_total=10/15=2/3 A.
The magnitude of the Ampere force:
F=BIl=0.6×(2/3)×0.15=0.06 N.
Its component upward along the inclined plane is
F cos30°=0.06×(√3/2)≈0.06×0.85=0.051 N.
The component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is
mg sin30°=0.17×0.5=0.085 N.
Since mg sin30° > F cos30°, the metal rod has a tendency to slide downward along the inclined plane, so the direction of static friction is upward along the inclined plane, with magnitude
f=mg sin30°−F cos30°=0.085−0.051=0.034 N.
